MapGatewayDelivery.report:
Scope and evidence discipline
Only the five requested targets were inspected. No edits, commands, tests, builds, gates, formatting, commits or network probes were performed. docs/upgrade-plan-desk-v2.md is outside those five targets, so this is a complete capability/evidence matrix for the requested n4 concerns and n3 dependencies, not a claim to have independently checked the literal numbered §12 steps. Parent should join this matrix to its already-read plan criteria. Line references below are actual source locations; historical receipt claims are distinguished from new execution.

Implementation coverage matrix

1. Seat endpoints / roster contracts — implemented in source, not live acceptance proven. Rosters.load (rosters.py:85–140) loads eight core tools plus seven seat-specific tools for each seat: all seven effective rosters are 15 tools. It checks seat mapping, endpoint, duplicates, 10–15 band, gate requirements and pack name/count. SeatServer._surface/list_tools/call_tool (server.py:81–145) restricts listed and dispatched names to the authenticated seat surface. SeatRouter (server.py:152–202) rejects a valid token for another seat with actual HTTP 403 and checks pack.seats. Pack surfaces are separate connectors and do not merge core tools. Rosters.surface (rosters.py:144–157) caps merged surfaces at 20. app_tools_load (tools/packs.py:17–39) checks seat eligibility and projected ceiling before persisting. Pack records carry task_id but are seat-global and remain until explicit unload (store.py:78–107); no ticket-close expiry exists.

2. OAuth / isolation — real authorization-code and refresh implementations exist. SeatOAuthProvider (oauth.py:91–354) persists DCR clients/access/refresh tokens in oauth-state.json, mode 0600 via replace; pending consents and authorization codes are memory-only. Consent uses constant-time passphrase lookup (config.py:104–113), chooses exactly one seat, expires after 600 s and locks after five wrong attempts (oauth.py:34–35, 207–237). It requires a PKCE challenge, stores it on a 600 s single-use authorization code; PKCE verifier processing is delegated to the MCP auth library, not implemented in this file. Tokens default to 24 h access / 30 d refresh, refresh rotates and rejects scope escalation (oauth.py:275–294). Static Grok clients accept HTTPS or loopback HTTP redirect URIs (oauth.py:58–72). Connector passphrases also act as non-expiring bearer tokens (oauth.py:296–307; server.py:219–231). MCP requires scope mcp but disables token resource validation (server.py:243–249); seat-path equality is the actual seat isolation boundary. This is not upstream row-level isolation: Hindsight uses configured per-seat bank names, while substrate fallback memory_search receives only query/limit (tools/core.py:106–122), not a seat-bank restriction.

3. Schemas / secrets — partial schema implementation. schema.validate (schema.py:37–93) enforces primitive types, enum, lengths, regex, numeric bounds, array limits/items, required fields, defaults and additionalProperties:false. It does not interpret oneOf/not, which androidmetavr_ui_tap actually declares (androidmetavr.yaml:99–103), nor format:uri. ios-local.yaml:45–47 explicitly documents absence of combinators and expects a backend semantic rejection, but that backend is absent. server.py:115–122 refuses credential-shaped serialized arguments and redacts results; credential detection is shape-based rather than arbitrary secret discovery. No new security policy beyond the requested contract is proposed.

4. Timeouts — implemented outer deadline, not universal work cancellation. config.py:28 sets 20 s; server.py:126–130 wraps backend dispatch. HttpUpstream uses bounded per-request clients (upstreams.py:78–109); substrate MCP uses asyncio.timeout (149–185). run_command cancels/reaps the process group on timeout or cancellation (upstreams.py:593–673). Timescale.query (upstreams.py:274–309) runs synchronous psycopg in asyncio.to_thread with connection timeout 5 s and read-only transaction default, but no SQL statement_timeout: canceling the await does not stop an already-running query thread. AgentBus.wait_job can poll for the requested 180 s default, yet desk_bus_wait_job is still cut off at the outer 20 s deadline (tools/lead.py:316–320; upstreams.py:214–225). Similarly gate calls carry 60/120 s inner budgets, prompt assembly 60 s, approval clone 90 s, all under 20 s. Parent must reconcile behavior with the plan's deadline contract, not simply increase all timeouts.

5. Audit — real local mirror and best-effort substrate emission, not every attempted call. Audit.tool_event (audit.py:29–62) appends tool.call with seat, tool, outcome, elapsed time, redacted argument digest and g5/g6 fields; fire_and_forget/send (64–78) asynchronously POST substrate /events with a six-second budget and only logging on failures. server.py returns before Audit.tool_event for forbidden surface, unknown tool, invalid schema and secret-refused arguments (108–122), so README's 'every call' is broader than code. No event replay/acknowledged remote durability is implemented; this observation is not a request for additional telemetry scope. Explicit event_emit locally records before attempting substrate (core.py:181–196).

6. Storage / n3 dependency — JSON, not Timescale index-of-record. Store._read/_write (store.py:32–48) tolerates unreadable/corrupt JSON by returning defaults, writes .tmp then replace with mode 0600, and uses a single-process RLock. There is no fsync or cross-process locking/transaction. roster, packs, intake, ack delivery, contract acks and doctor all use this Store. The file header explicitly says Timescale migration is future work (store.py:3–5). Timescale.query is SELECT/WITH-only and transaction-read-only; no write schema or mutation path is present. Dragonfly is bounded-TTL cache only; systems.cache namespaces keys with seat (tools/systems.py:33–37). Configured read adapters do not prove migrations, data import or substrate schema deployment. Minimal n3→n4 contract: establish authoritative storage schema and transactions for these currently persisted shapes, including origin-scoped intake idempotency and write-ahead per-ack delivery markers, then switch callers without a parallel shadow authority.

7. Doctor / bootstrap — partial verification and prompt rendering. core.doctor (199–255) permits registering self UUID, and channel registration only by LEAD. install_prompt/repair return an assembled prompt and SHA plus installation hint; they do not write a bot container's prompt. render_prompt (276–324) requires all seven UUIDs and channel, exports configured main, runs the existing assembler and rejects leftover placeholders. check compares caller-supplied prompt SHA to stored expected SHA, caller-supplied installed_skills to declared names, and tests memory/substrate health plus roster counts. Connector is marked green because this call authenticated. Roster green only checks seven UUIDs and nonempty channel; quality_in_channel:false is hardcoded (core.py:246). lead.roster_status also derives in_channel from seat name (lead.py:323–351). Neither checks real channel membership nor actual installed files. Thus these outputs cannot prove fresh-desk acceptance without independent bot/container evidence.

8. Intake and contract acknowledgements — implemented locally. /v1/intake (server.py:306–336) accepts origin-token auth, origin match, schema and title/ask secret checks, then persists intake and emits handoff. Static seat passphrases get 403; an OAuth seat token is not recognized as origin and falls through to 401, despite README's blanket seat-token-403 claim. Store.intake_create (109–134) deduplicates by origin plus idempotency_key; next atomically claims first queued item in one process (136–151). Only LEAD has next/ack. lead.intake_ack/_reply_once (35–170) posts GitHub-origin callbacks before state advance, writes delivery marker before posting, uses digest-keyed per-ack process-local lock, reads comment markers on ambiguous attempts, and refuses notify_unknown when outcome cannot be proven. GitHub-unconfigured first attempts may still persist ack with delivered:false. Non-GitHub origins have no callback (lead.py:230–238). quality.contract_ack/status (213–241) replaces each seat's ack, reads consumers_required from proposal YAML and reports missing/rejected; records are JSON, not durable substrate/Timescale contract registry. No inspected path automatically mirrors acknowledgement into a version-controlled change document.

Declared tool-family coverage

Core eight: desk_brief, docs_search, memory_retain, memory_recall, ownership_resolve, receipt_check, event_emit, doctor → tools/core.py:19,49,81,106,125,161,181,199. Brief caches 300 s only after substrate succeeds; task_id is used for recall/cache but substrate brief gets repo=None and graph_id only. RAGFlow retrieval returns content/document/dataset/score (core.py:49–78), not the source commit promised in _core.yaml:31–34. Retain requires receipt_path or source and marks substrate memory agent-claimed; it does not validate cited evidence contents.
LEAD seven: intake_next/ack, graph_register/state, bus_start/wait, roster_status → tools/lead.py:28,35,254,267,306,316,323. graph_state translates claim/release/complete/heartbeat, heartbeat requires lease_id; complete intentionally sends tests_pass:false rather than manufacturing verification. Claim/release/complete return ok:true after transport success without heartbeat's explicit semantic ok:false check.
SYSTEMS seven: index_query/events_query/cache/lsp_diagnostics/contract_propose/design_artifact_get/app_tools_load → systems.py:19,26,33,51,73,183 plus packs.py:17. SQL is SELECT/WITH plus keyword/one-statement filtering; Timescale adds read-only transaction. LSP shells to the configured repository's broker; no broker execution was performed here. contract_propose builds proposal bundle/branch/draft PR or honestly returns an unpushed bundle.
WEB seven: lsp_diagnostics, vercel_deployments/promote/rollback, preview_check, bundle_secret_scan, contract_ack → systems.py:51; web.py:24,41,50,59,86; quality.py:213. Vercel has configured project allowlist. preview_check refuses redirects by not following any redirect. No g5 approval validation exists.
ANDROID seven: play_track_status/staged_rollout/halt_rollout, artifact_size_delta, lint_baseline_diff, contract_ack, app_tools_load → mobile.py:18,32,100,128,141; quality.py:213; packs.py:17. Staged rollout reads and preserves existing releases; halt_threshold is echoed, not monitored automatically. Production 100% authorization is merely substring 'full' in approval_id (mobile.py:37–38).
iOS seven: testflight_status/appstore_phased_release/pause_release, entitlements_diff, review_risk_check, contract_ack, app_tools_load → mobile.py:176,196,217,241,267; quality.py:213; packs.py:17. ASC resolves bundle-specific app before version. Risk check is diff-pattern classification, not actual App Review acceptance; halt_signal is echoed rather than watched.
INFRA seven: railway_status/logs/variable_names/redeploy, tailscale_status, vps_units, db_health → infra.py:49,102,129,139,185 and corresponding later functions. Redeploy checks current deployment equals supplied prior_deployment_id in selected production/default environment, then mutates; this is staleness protection, not approval authorization.
QUALITY seven: gates_run, greptile_review, receipt_approve, waiver_record, contract_ack_status, supply_chain_check, secret_scan → quality.py:23,115,136,192,220,244,263. Gates use trusted installed scripts and refuse partial success when no receipt. supply_chain_check explicitly says license/CVE lookup is not wired (259); current output only identifies changed lockfiles/manifests, unpinned tokens and git dependencies.

All eight packs
kanbanos (5), desklanes (5), clippyos (4): WEB/ANDROID/iOS; real packs.py functions for health, query, test push, flags, crashes, scoreboard, store listing, render job. Product bases are only configured for these three (config.py:134–138). Required product API contracts: GET /health, POST /desk/query, POST /desk/push-test, GET /desk/flags, /desk/crashes, /api/scoreboard, /desk/store-listing, /api/render-jobs/<id>. Pack HTTP adapter provides no configured authorization headers; test-device-only is forwarded as test_only:true rather than locally checking a registry. api_smoke calls only /health although KanbanOS description promises contract endpoint and Desk Lanes promises scoreboard too.
coordination (2): SYSTEMS and LEAD; real systems.graph_heartbeat/drift_scan (systems.py:190–229). Calls substrate graph_heartbeat and coord_drift_scan; heartbeat rejects semantic ok:false as lease_rejected. Live behavior/signatures not proven by the receipt.
androidlocal (5): emulator boot, adb devices, APK install, unit test, instrumented run → android_cli.* missing.
androidmetavr (4): logcat, screenshot, UI dump, UI tap → android_cli.* missing. Header lines 13–22 explicitly says underlying MetaVR bridge only resolves IDs, performs no MCP/network invocation, hardcodes connected=false and always raises DeviceUnavailable. This is documented upstream prerequisite, not a claim independently confirmed outside scope.
ioslocal (5): plist lint, entitlements scan, Linux SPM test, snapshot diff, xcodebuild receipt → ios.* missing.
iosmetavr (3): screenshot, UI dump, tap → ios.* missing; contract says executable lookup may honestly skip when unavailable, and directed tap cannot be honored until underlying CLI adds target (ios-metavr.yaml:54–66).
Missing modules were established from the complete tools directory listing plus contract/backend search. Resolver import_module (tools/__init__.py:97–103) raises ModuleNotFoundError, which server's generic handler converts to internal, not backend_missing. Contracts can list unavailable tools successfully because loader does not resolve backends.

Approvals: two distinct deficiencies
A. g5/g6 approval_id: rosters._tool (64–68) enforces required field names only; runtime schema checks string length, not issuer/actor/resource/action authorization. Audit records claimed ID and rollback plan. infra.py:149–150 explicitly declares approval unverified by design, and output repeats this at 181. web/mobile mutations likewise only echo it; Android's 'full' substring is no trusted authorization. Minimal dependency: authoritative approval lookup bound to actor/seat, permitted action and target, plus genuine externally issued approval record; do not synthesize IDs or treat existing audit as approval. This is a code gap plus real external approval prerequisite.
B. receipt approval / exact SHA: quality.receipt_approve reads tip, prevents QUALITY self-approval, stamps approved_by/approved_at, validates stamped candidate with strict G-2/G-3/G-5–6 and commits using expect_sha/content (136–189). _commit_file compares cloned tip/content, then atomically pushes with force-with-lease against found_sha (296–390): real TOCTOU protection exists. But there is no approval_ref input or assignment anywhere in the inspected gateway/contracts, and no reference tying independent approval to reviewed exact source SHA. Branch-tip conditional push is not exact-SHA independent approval. repo.resolve_ref (66–75) falls back to HEAD even for an explicit unresolved ref; historical TOCTOU receipt itself acknowledges this. Minimal dependency: independent reviewer-approved exact SHA/reference contract, persisted binding and strict unresolved-ref behavior; real reviewer approval cannot be supplied by code or this agent.

Receipts and external blockers
- desk-v2-gateway.json records 40 gateway tests/119 gate tests but explicitly only not_configured upstream paths and in-process OAuth, no real Grok card. Its outside-receipt smoke assertion is not evidence here.
- trusted-gates and ack/Railway receipts explicitly say no restart/deploy and no upstream calls; tests use stubs/fake HTTP. Privilege dropping was not exercised.
- TOCTOU receipt records local bare-remote tests, approved_by empty, no approval_ref.
- coordination receipt records 114 tests and skip-clean smoke only; fabricated success/rejection response bodies, live signatures and integration unverified. approved_by is bot-00-programming-lead but approval_ref absent; that field alone does not satisfy exact-SHA approval.
- None of the inspected receipts establish production health, real Grok OAuth, real bot prompt installation, actual channel membership, Timescale write migration, data-plane ingress or live platform mutation authorization.
External prerequisites versus code: network forwarders/data-plane availability and credentials; substrate/bus tokens and real API signatures; Railway project IDs/token; Vercel team/project allowlist/token; Greptile/GitHub credentials; Play access token; ASC key/issuer/key file plus JWT dependency; product API bases implementing listed routes; actual mobile device/MetaVR executables and underlying unavailable-device/directed-tap capability; seven real bot UUIDs/channel and installed prompt/skills; independent exact-SHA review and genuine deploy/destructive approvals. Parent-supplied observations about DNS/forwarders/unregistered seats remain blockers without rerunning checks. Credentials alone do not fix JSON authority, missing adapters, ignored schema constraints or missing approval authorization.

Suggested planning dependency order (contracts only, no extra scope)
First join parent n3 schema/API decisions to the gateway Store shapes and event API. Next settle authoritative approval_id and exact-SHA approval_ref contracts with the independent reviewer; implement checks before exposing write-class platform mutations. Then implement missing declared mobile adapters against real CLI/device contracts, complete explicitly promised outputs (supply-chain lookup and pack smoke endpoints), and correct validation/doctor provenance. Finally parent runs its one verification wave and obtains real connector/upstream/fresh-desk evidence plus independent approval. No newly executed verification is claimed in this report.

MapShareAndNetworkDelivery.report:
## Scope and evidence rules
Read-only investigation of infra/, grokbot/, scripts/, skills/, and .receipts/bot-05-infrastructure, plus only concrete plan/gate/workflow/prompt/doctor sources needed to explain those artifacts. No build, test, lint, formatter, gate, smoke, git, deployment or state-changing command was executed. Historical receipt command results below are records, not fresh observations. Conclusions about missing packaging/publication evidence are bounded to these inspected paths. No external repository was inspected or changed. D-1/D-2/D-3 preserved; D-4 is the original authoring-session restriction, not an ongoing invented prohibition.

## n2: six-step network coverage
1. Ultrathink forwarder: infra/railway/forwarders.yaml:7–16 specifies production machine ultrathink-production-tailscale-forwarder and 4000/4001/4003 → greptimedb.railway.internal at matching ports, 5432 → timescaledb.railway.internal:5432, 6379 → dragonfly.railway.internal:6379. These are real authored mappings, explicitly provisional service names, NOT discovered deployed services.
2. Agent Substrate forwarder: same file:18–24 specifies agent-substrate-production-tailscale-forwarder, 8888 → hindsight-api.railway.internal:8888, 9380 → ragflow.railway.internal:9380 and optional 80 → ragflow.railway.internal:80. infra/railway/README.md:20–62 documents reusable tagged TS_AUTHKEY, ephemeral off, preapproval when needed, deployment into each production environment, /var/lib/tailscale state volume and manually disabling resulting machine key expiry. Neither file contains applied Railway IDs or deployment evidence.
3. ACL: infra/tailscale/policy.hujson:19–33 gives autogroup:admin ownership of tag:railway-forwarder/tag:vps/tag:admin and the sole grant from VPS/admin to forwarders. Everything else is denied absent another grant. Lines 36–51 declare accepted mapped ports and denied SSH/public-service directions. Concrete discrepancy: tcp:4000-4003 at line 32 includes TCP 4002 even though forwarders.yaml declares only 4000,4001,4003; the comment 'Exactly the forwarded ports' is therefore inaccurate. This is an authored least-privilege gap, not an observed live ACL. README:64–79 lists VPS probes and only repeat tailscale ping from Mac mini; it does not provide recorded Mac application-port probes. The example omits explicit 4001 and optional 80 probes, so it cannot alone establish every mapped port.
4. Env cutover: README:81–87 requires changing both substrate and gateway env names, restarting both units, then checking /brief/events_emit/health. infra/substrate/SUBSTRATE-ENV.md:59–94 prefers MagicDNS but documents a historical public HTTPS + Basic fallback after a tailnet startup timeout. Lines 146–153 require root-owned 0600 dated file backup, restart, desk_db_health/events_emit/desk_brief and names-only diff receipt. infra/substrate/substrate.env.example:20–47 leaves real values absent and explicitly documents that fallback. Historical Phase A receipt says GREPTIME_URL remained public and no network cutover was performed in that change.
5. G-6 retire exposure: README:89–102 requires recorded approval BEFORE removing Timescale TCP proxy and Greptime public domain, removal CLI/screenshot evidence, and recreation rollback. New TCP proxy gets a new public port; affected consumers must be updated. Optional Hindsight UI public exposure is an Ove choice, not silently included. No removal approval/removal evidence appeared in the inspected infrastructure receipts.
6. Required network receipt: desk-v2-infra.json:100–105 explicitly says ACL not applied/validated and forwarders specified, not deployed. Its commands cover ownership/secrets/contracts, shell/YAML/systemd syntax and INFRA source XML only. They do not prove Tailscale status, any deployed port, app-level call, Mac access or public exposure retirement.

External n2 gates remain: n1's actual project/service/env inventory; valid private tagged key; deployed persistent forwarders and expiry state; applied exact-port ACL; VPS and Mac evidence; successful substrate/gateway cutover; human G-6 approval and actual proxy/domain deletion/recovery references. Parent-provided current observation that named forwarders are absent corroborates noncompletion but was not re-probed here.

## Gateway install and CI/intake activation dependencies
infra/desk-gateway/install.sh:20–80 canonicalizes /opt/programming-desk, using rsync -a --delete for updates; lines 149–163 preserve existing env, create a names-only 0600 template when absent, migrate DESK_REPO_DIR and warn against premature DESK_GATE_USER. Lines 165–215 sync dependencies, adjust traversal permissions, check desk-gate interpreter/readability, install unit, enable/restart and request loopback health. Existence of this installer does not mean these actions occurred. infra/desk-gateway/install-nginx.sh:15–39 installs HTTP/SSL config but enables SSL only when certificate exists; prints certbot rather than issuing it. DNS to VPS and certificate issuance/re-run are external activation steps. Initial receipt explicitly says DNS/cert/vhosts not active at its recording time; that historical statement must not replace current observation.

.github/workflows/gates.yml:24–39 has PR-to-main and push-main triggers. gates is PR-only, both jobs use [self-hosted,Linux,X64]. ## Scope and evidence rules
Read-only investigation restricted to the five requested companion paths. No context-file search, runtime commands, builds, tests, gates, edits, commits or pushes. Source references below are relative to /root/src/repos/agent-substrate. Negative findings are bounded to those inspected paths, using broad symbol searches plus alternate DDL/adapter/projector searches. No claim is made about code in other packages or installed agents. The Desk plan itself was outside the five-path scope; matrix covers every n3 deliverable named in this assignment, without inventing additional §12 step names.

## Package boundaries and safe consumption
1. Consume the companion as an external substrate service using its existing REST /brief and /events or MCP /mcp contracts (server.ts), not by importing CLI modules. Respect the event response stored flag: normalized/hash-bearing output is not a persisted receipt. Direct PG/Greptime/Dragonfly access by Desk seats would bypass the documented single-writer boundary.
2. planes.ts exports small low-level clients, but @substrate/mcp-server is private and its main boots src/index.ts; there is no declared standalone adapter package/export contract. A deep import would couple Desk to companion source layout and Bun/runtime dependencies. Prefer a Desk-owned boundary over explicit configured service contracts rather than copying the incomplete companion implementation.
3. @substrate/projector package.json main points to src/index.ts, but the complete source listing contains only cursor.ts and substrate-yaml-projector.ts. Both execute immediately on load. Do not import/run them as a reusable Grok Bot plugin library. Generate into a private staged destination only after parent validates supported plugin/config shape; preserve unrelated agent config with managed ownership and real rollback.
4. Existing projector prints resolved token values to stdout, writes with default filesystem mode rather than explicit 0600, lacks shell escaping, and catches filesystem write errors while continuing to a success-style completion message. No invocation should receive production credentials or target live configs until these issues are addressed in the owning integration. Parsing a YAML version does not validate supported version.
5. Do not alter companion .planning or adopt its archived phases as Desk milestones. Parent's Desk n1–n7 graph remains authoritative; attach specific source capabilities to it, explicitly tracking missing real behavior and external receipts rather than accepting archival completion labels.
